title: utilz install publishes without consulting or recording the gates CI runs
body:
## Summary

`utilz install` publishes an install by running `cargo build --release` and nothing else. It never consults the gates CI runs, so **the publish path cannot refuse what CI would refuse**, and a published install carries no record of which gates were green when it was cut.

## How it shipped

On 2026-09-09, `vc` published an install from commit `b6ca749` while that commit's clippy gate was red -- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` exited 101 on two errors introduced by ST0017/WP-01. `install.sh` refuses a dirty tree (`:582`, `:733`) and has no flag to override that (`:736`), so it is not indifferent to tree state; it is indifferent to *gate* state.

**The install itself was correct, and that is the point rather than the mitigation.** It was verified by behaviour -- provenance `b6ca749`, both invocation forms answering, and 0 of 15 `opt/*/README.md` carrying an absolute home path where 8 had before. **Nothing in the publish path could have told anyone if it had not been.** A publish that happens to be correct and a publish that is verified produce the same install.

## Why this is filed rather than fixed inline

A defect that shipped earns an issue even when the fix lands inside a steel thread (hv, 2026-07-29 precedent). This shipped: there is a published install in `/Users/matts/Devel/opt/utilz` cut from a red commit, and `utilz` on PATH resolves to it.

## Severity

Medium. The failure is silent rather than destructive, and the two-tree estate is exactly where checkout-green and install-correct come apart. `utilz test` refuses from an install and every bats suite pins `UTILZ_HOME` from `test_helper.bash`, so **no existing suite is structurally capable of measuring a published install** -- which leaves the publish path as the only place this could be caught, and it does not look.

## The fix hv ratified, 2026-09-09

**Record gate state in the manifest rather than blocking on it.** `manifest.sha256` already carries `utilz-version`, `source-commit` and `source-tree`, so gate state is a small extension of a record that exists rather than a new mechanism.

Chosen over running the full gate set at publish time, which is correct and slow, and over leaving it alone. **Recording makes a bad publish visible without making every publish expensive** -- and visibility is the property that was missing, not refusal.

Open, deliberately, for whoever takes it: whether a later `utilz install` should *refuse* when the recorded state is red, or merely report it. Recording first is what makes that decision measurable.

## SCHEDULED 2026-09-09: A WP-05 RIDER, RECORD-ONLY (vc recommended, hv agreed)

**Not now, and not a special trip.** `manifest.sha256` is inside WP-05's own scope -- *command
surface: shim dispatch, manifest, help, doctor* -- so recording gate state there costs almost
nothing extra, where taking it today interrupts cc mid-WP-03.

**Why this one is worth building where issue 0019 was not, since both were about an incomplete
record.** 0019's information already existed: `git show --stat` names every file in every commit.
**This information exists NOWHERE.** `manifest.sha256` carries `utilz-version`, `source-commit` and
`source-tree` and no gate state; `utilz test` refuses from an install; and every bats suite pins
`UTILZ_HOME` from `test_helper.bash`, so no existing suite is structurally capable of measuring a
published install. A publish that happens to be correct and a publish that is verified produce the
same install, and nothing in the estate can tell them apart.

**RECORD ONLY. The refuse-or-report question stays open**, deliberately -- it is not answerable
until there is a record to measure, which is the whole reason recording comes first.
